title.narrative: Emergency response to Sudan crisis - South Sudan returnees and IDPs in Upper Nile

description.narrative: Upper Nile State: sharing the largest border with Sudan is receiving the biggest number of the people fleeing the conflict in Sudan through the border entry point at Joda, north of Renk town. People have been entering Upper Nile State in tens of thousands from the onset of the conflict until today. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in partnership with the Government provided transport to tens of thousands of people. The Catholic diocese of Malakal, through its Caritas Office, provided transport to about 4,000 people mostly from Upper Nile State. The great challenge in the State is now short-term humanitarian support to the returnees who reached their home areas and intend to resettle. Caritas Malakal has received multiple appeals from the following locations: Malakal transit camp where 8,000 returnees are hosted, Kodok (Fashoda County), where more than 10,000 returnees have resettled and Wadakona (Manyo County), where 7,000 returnees have resettled. The conditions of most of the returnees are of high vulnerability. “The main needs identified are food, nutrition and health services, Shelter and NFIs, Clean water and sanitation, core relief items for women and girls “. The commissioner of Kodok, reiterated the same needs during a visit CTP and Caritas Malakal made in November 2023. It is very important to intervene now because, as the emergency continues, people who fled the conflict in Sudan have lost all belongings and require basic human needs in order to survive, among which are food, shelter, protection services and to support resettle them once the returnees reach their home areas, for instance Kodok and Wadakona
